For agreements of 3 years or less
raw_claim_replay.quote:
Mandatory break fees may apply, which are payable based on the stage of the agreement.

If the mandatory break fee applies, the set fee payable is:

*   4 weeks' rent if less than 25 per cent of the agreement has expired
*   3 weeks' rent if 25 per cent or more but less than 50 per cent of the agreement has expired
*   2 weeks' rent if 50 per cent or more but less than 75 per cent of the agreement has expired
*   1 week's rent if 75 per cent or more of the agreement has expired.

raw_claim_replay.text: For fixed-term agreements longer than 3 years signed before 23 March 2020, the optional break fee clause applies automatically unless deleted, and it specifies either 6 or 4 weeks’ rent — not a four-tier structure.
section_path: When break fees apply
Tenant breaking a fixed-term agreement signed before 23 March 2020
If the optional break fee is included in agreement
raw_claim_replay.quote:
The optional break fee clause will apply if the break fee clause has not been deleted from the tenancy agreement. The break fee payable will be either:

*   6 weeks rent if the tenant leaves in the first half of the fixed-term agreement, or
*   4 weeks rent if the tenant leaves in the second half of the fixed-term agreement.

The same optional break fee clause applies for fixed-term agreements of more than 3 years, unless the tenancy agreement specifies a break fee of another amount.

raw_claim_replay.quote:
The landlord or agent may negotiate an agreed amount of compensation for their costs with the tenant.

These costs may include loss of rent, advertising, and a letting fee if the landlord uses an agent.

If the tenant and landlord are unable to agree on the amount of compensation, the landlord may claim from the bond or [apply to the NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal](https://www.ncat.nsw.gov.au/ncat/case-types/housing-and-property/tenancy.html "Apply for help resolving your dispute at NCAT (https://www.ncat.nsw.gov.au/ncat/case-types/housing-and-property/tenancy.html)") (the Tribunal) for an order that the tenant pays the landlord a certain amount of compensation.

The landlord will need to show the Tribunal what (reasonable) steps they took to minimise their losses (e.g. advertising for a new tenant without delay).

accepted_claim.text:
Source context: Getting your bond back at the end of a tenancy > What do you need to do?

If a co-tenant moves out of a shared tenancy and requests their bond refund, the remaining tenant/s must pay back their bond – less any rent owed or other reasonable costs – within 14 days of the request.
accepted_claim.quote: If a co-tenant moves out of a shared tenancy and requests their bond refund, the remaining tenant/s must pay back their bond – less any rent owed or other reasonable costs – within 14 days of the request.

remaining_semantic_risks.missing_adjacent_source:
This does not apply if:

*   the former co-tenant’s debts exceed the amount of bond money they paid, or
*   the former co-tenant has been excluded from the premises by a final apprehended violence order.
remaining_semantic_risks.explanation: Repayment within 14 days is quoted without immediately following exceptions for former tenant debt exceeding share or exclusion by final apprehended violence order. Exact quotation preservation cannot restore unselected adjacent conditions. Gold expected_conditions already mentions these exceptions; current regex does not detect their omission.

remaining_semantic_risks.explanation: Quote ends with should and contains no submit/respond action. Correct action is in next bullet list, selected by another claim. Answer-level source context supports the conclusion, but this claim’s own quotation is incomplete. Guard only catches colon/dangling conjunction lead-ins.

limitations: No gold or production changes were made during this audit.
Four language-policy regex mismatches remain reported as failures; they were not silently rescored.
Zero literal-citation failures is not proof of condition coverage or entailment.
The source-preserving fallback can expose long duplicated source sections and preserve English in a Chinese conversation; this is intentional conservative behavior with a usability cost.
